sagePrompts.title: App Intro
sagePrompts.prompt: Sage, please introduce me to the "Scholar's Dungeon" application. What are its core mechanics, reward systems, and how should I start my journey of growth here?

sagePrompts.title: Create Tasks
sagePrompts.prompt: Help me plan an expedition. Please create a structured learning task or expedition for me, including its tiers, required tasks, and rewards.

sagePrompts.title: Balance Guide
sagePrompts.prompt: Based on my current level, gold earning rate, and shop prices, could you recommend how I should set my game balance? For example, how should XP and Gold rewards for each Focus Session be distributed to be fair and motivating?

sagePrompts.title: Weekly Analysis
sagePrompts.prompt: Please retrieve my study records from the past 7 days and analyze my peak focus hours, as well as the correlation between my emotional state and productivity. Please summarize my overall performance this week using intuitive data observations.

sagePrompts.title: Monthly Review
sagePrompts.prompt: I would like to do a deep reflection on the past month. Please analyze my monthly progress curve. Have I stagnated in any area? Based on my growth rate, please set three specific "step-by-step goals" for next month.

sagePrompts.title: Efficiency
sagePrompts.prompt: Please analyze my recent learning efficiency trends and provide three practical and actionable suggestions for improvement.

sagePrompts.title: Encouragement
sagePrompts.prompt: I have been feeling a bit exhausted lately. Please give me some encouragement and motivation.

messages.content: How should I balance finishing the Triton kernel ablations with drafting Chapter 3 of my thesis this week?

A dual-block rhythm works best here:

1. **Morning High-Cognition Block (08:30–12:00 at Lab)**: Dedicate 2–3 sessions to *Implement Block-Sparse Attention Kernel* and launch long-running ablation jobs before lunch.
2. **Afternoon Synthesis Block (14:00–17:30 at Library)**: While GPU jobs run, switch to *Draft Methodology & Architecture Figures* so your writing captures fresh experimental details without context-switching overhead.
